theorem pow2_coprime_odd (k : ℕ) {m : ℕ} (hm : m % 2 = 1) :
    Nat.Coprime (2 ^ k) m :=
  Nat.Coprime.pow_left k (Nat.coprime_two_right.mpr (Nat.odd_iff.mpr hm))
annotations.title: Powers of 2 are coprime to odd numbers
annotations.body: The fundamental coprimality result: 2^k and any odd number m have gcd 1. The proof chains three Mathlib lemmas: Nat.odd_iff converts the mod-2 condition to the Odd predicate, Nat.coprime_two_right.mpr gives Nat.Coprime 2 m when m is odd, and Nat.Coprime.pow_left lifts this to 2^k.

annotations.lean:
theorem pow2_not_coprime_pow2 {k j : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hj : 1 ≤ j) :
    ¬ Nat.Coprime (2 ^ k) (2 ^ j)
annotations.title: Two positive powers of 2 are never coprime
annotations.body: The uniqueness constraint: any two distinct powers of 2 share factor 2. Since 2 ∣ 2^k and 2 ∣ 2^j for k, j ≥ 1, we have 2 ∣ gcd(2^k, 2^j), so gcd ≥ 2 > 1. This explains why an RNS base can contain at most one power of 2.

annotations.lean:
structure Pow2RNSBase where
  power : ℕ
  oddMods : List ℕ
  power_pos : 1 ≤ power
  mods_ge_three : ∀ m ∈ oddMods, 3 ≤ m
  mods_odd : ∀ m ∈ oddMods, m % 2 = 1
  mods_coprime : oddMods.Pairwise Nat.Coprime
annotations.title: The Pow2RNSBase structure
annotations.body: A valid power-of-2 RNS base has one power-of-2 channel (exponent ≥ 1) and a list of odd channels (each ≥ 3, pairwise coprime). The constraints ensure: (1) the power-of-2 channel is ≥ 2, (2) each odd channel is a valid RNS channel, (3) the odd channels are mutually coprime. Together with pow2_coprime_odd, this makes the full list pairwise coprime.

annotations.title: A Pow2RNSBase gives a pairwise coprime list
annotations.body: The full moduli list [2^power, m₁, ..., mₙ] is pairwise coprime. Proof uses List.Pairwise.cons: the head (2^power) is coprime to each mᵢ via pow2_coprime_odd (since each mᵢ is odd by mods_odd), and the tail is pairwise coprime by mods_coprime.

annotations.lean:
theorem Pow2RNSBase.dynamicRange_eq (b : Pow2RNSBase) :
    b.toRNSBase.dynamicRange = 2 ^ b.power * b.oddMods.prod
annotations.title: Dynamic range formula for power-of-2 RNS base
annotations.body: The dynamic range (product of all moduli) factors as 2^power times the product of the odd moduli. For {4, 3, 5, 7}: range = 4 × 3 × 5 × 7 = 420. For {16, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13}: range = 16 × 15015 = 240240. The factored form makes the dependence on k explicit.

annotations.lean:
theorem base_4_3_5_7_coprime : [4, 3, 5, 7].Pairwise Nat.Coprime := by decide
theorem base_4_3_5_7_range : [4, 3, 5, 7].prod = 420 := by norm_num
annotations.title: The base {4, 3, 5, 7}: range 420
annotations.body: A concrete 4-channel RNS base with a power-of-2 channel: 4 = 2², with odd channels 3, 5, 7. Dynamic range 420. Compare with the prime base {2, 3, 5, 7} (range 210): replacing 2 with 4 doubles the range with the same channel count.

annotations.lean:
theorem base_16_3_5_7_11_13_coprime :
    [16, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13].Pairwise Nat.Coprime := by decide
theorem base_16_3_5_7_11_13_range : [16, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13].prod = 240240 := by norm_num
annotations.title: The base {16, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13}: range 240240
annotations.body: A 6-channel RNS base: 16 = 2⁴, with the first 5 odd primes. Dynamic range 240240. A hardware implementation would compute mod-16 via a 4-bit AND mask, while the 5 odd channels use standard modular arithmetic. The large range (up to 240240 representable values) makes this base suitable for DSP applications.

annotations.title: Replacing 2 with 4 doubles the dynamic range
annotations.body: For the same 4 channels and same channel count, using 4 = 2² instead of 2 doubles the dynamic range from 210 to 420. This illustrates the general principle: replacing 2^j with 2^k (j < k) multiplies the range by 2^(k-j). The hardware overhead of the power-of-2 channel is essentially the same (bitwise AND with a wider mask).

annotations.lean:
theorem base_2_4_invalid : ¬ [2, 4].Pairwise Nat.Coprime := by decide
theorem base_4_8_invalid : ¬ [4, 8].Pairwise Nat.Coprime := by decide
annotations.title: Two powers of 2 make an invalid base
annotations.body: Concrete witnesses for the uniqueness constraint. gcd(2, 4) = 2 ≠ 1 and gcd(4, 8) = 4 ≠ 1. These are verified by decide (kernel computation). The general case is proved by pow2_not_coprime_pow2.

annotations.lean:
theorem pow2_bit_length (k : ℕ) : Nat.log 2 (2 ^ k) = k :=
  Nat.log_pow (by norm_num : 1 < 2) k
annotations.title: Hardware bit-width of the power-of-2 channel
annotations.body: ⌊log₂(2^k)⌋ = k, confirming that the 2^k channel requires a k-bit AND mask for modular reduction. The reduction x mod 2^k = x &&& (2^k - 1) uses a k-bit mask. This is a single instruction on modern hardware, making the power-of-2 channel the cheapest RNS channel to implement.
